etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English tribut, from Old French tribut, from Latin tributum (“tribute”, literally “a thing contributed or paid”), neuter of tributus, past participle of tribuō (“to assign, allot”), usually derived from tribus (“tribe”). See tribe.

definitions.definition: An homage made in a body of work to another work or creator.
An acknowledgment of gratitude, respect or admiration; an accompanying gift.

quote.citation: 1750 June 12 (date written; published 1751), T[homas] Gray, “Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard”, in Designs by Mr. R[ichard] Bentley, for Six Poems by Mr. T. Gray, London:  […]  R[obert] Dodsley, […], published 1753, →OCLC:
quote.text: the passing tribute of a sigh

definitions.definition: A payment made by one nation to another in submission.
A payment made by a feudal vassal to his lord.
(mining) A certain proportion of the mined ore, or of its value, given to the miner as payment.

quote.citation: 1778, William Pryce, Mineralogia Cornubiensis: A Treatise on Minerals, Mines, and Mining […] :
quote.text: The setting of a Copper Mine upon tribute , has this difference : the Tributor is at the sole expence of digging , raising , and dressing , all the Ore that can be made merchantable

quote.citation: 1852-1866, Charles Tomlinson, Cyclopaedia of Useful Arts and Manufactures
quote.text: Tut-work is also employed upon the lode itself, though from the advantages generally considered to arise from the tribute system […]
Amorous Trifler, that spendeth […] his Afternoones in discourse with Paint, or Lust, tributing most precious Minutes, to the Scepter of a Fanne.
